precepts.text: The service of the sons of Kohath is about the most holy things; Aaron and his sons take down the covering vail and cover the ark before the camp sets forward.
precepts.point: The Kohathites were in charge of carrying the sanctuary to and fro, and the reading further on shows them doing it once the camp moved.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

precepts.why:
Gershon got two wagons and four oxen and Merari four wagons and eight oxen, “But unto the sons of Kohath he gave none: because the service of the sanctuary belonging unto them was that they should bear upon their shoulders.” Numbers 4 shows what that bearing was.

“This shall be the service of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation, about the most holy things: And when the camp setteth forward, Aaron shall come, and his sons, and they shall take down the covering vail, and cover the ark of testimony with it: And shall put thereon the covering of badgers’ skins, and shall spread over it a cloth wholly of blue, and shall put in the staves thereof.”

The service of the sons of Kohath is about the most holy things. Aaron and his sons covered the ark and the vessels first, and the staves were put in, because those things were carried on shoulders, not on wagons.

precepts.text: When Aaron has made an end of covering the sanctuary, the sons of Kohath come to bear it, but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die.
precepts.point: The Kohathites were in charge of carrying the sanctuary to and fro, and the reading further on shows them doing it once the camp moved.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

precepts.why:
“And when Aaron and his sons have made an end of covering the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, as the camp is to set forward; after that, the sons of Kohath shall come to bear it: but they shall not touch any holy thing, lest they die. These things are the burden of the sons of Kohath in the tabernacle of the congregation.”

That is why the sons of Kohath received no wagons and no oxen. Their burden was the sanctuary itself, borne on their shoulders once Aaron had covered it, and not touching any holy thing lest they die. The Kohathites were in charge of carrying the sanctuary to and fro, and the reading further on shows them doing it once the camp moved.

precepts.text: When Christ cometh into the world he saith, sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; he taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.
precepts.point: There is also no tabernacle today to do them at. The sacrifices had to be done at the tabernacle, and Israel is scattered everywhere in captivity, not able to go to Jerusalem to a temple that is not standing.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

precepts.why:
The dedication of the altar is summed up: twelve chargers of silver, twelve silver bowls, twelve spoons of gold, and all the bullocks, rams, lambs and goats for the burnt offering, the sin offering and the peace offerings. Israel does not do the animal sacrifices anymore.

“Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.” The Most High had no pleasure in them, because the people’s minds were not changed when they offered them.

“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” Christ was the ultimate sacrifice: “He taketh away the first, that he may establish the second.” The sacrifices offered by the law are the first; Christ took them away to establish the second.

There is also no tabernacle today to do them at. The sacrifices had to be done at the tabernacle, and Israel is scattered everywhere in captivity, not able to go to Jerusalem to a temple that is not standing.

precepts.text: There I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims.
precepts.point: When Moses was gone into the tabernacle of the congregation to speak with him, that is Moses going in to speak with the Most High. The voice came from off the mercy seat that was upon the ark of testimony, from between the two cherubims, exactly where the Lord said he would meet and commune with him.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

precepts.why:
When Moses went into the tabernacle of the congregation to speak with him, that is Moses going in to speak with the Most High. He heard the voice “from off the mercy seat that was upon the ark of testimony, from between the two cherubims”, exactly where the Lord said he would meet him.

“And thou shalt put the mercy seat above upon the ark; and in the ark thou shalt put the testimony that I shall give thee. And there I will meet with thee, and I will commune with thee from above the mercy seat, from between the two cherubims which are upon the ark of the testimony, of all things which I will give thee in commandment unto the children of Israel.”

What the Lord promised at Sinai, that he would meet and commune with Moses from above the mercy seat, is what happened in the tabernacle after the altar was dedicated.

points: On the day that Moses had fully set up the tabernacle and anointed and sanctified it with all the instruments thereof, the princes of Israel, heads of the house of their fathers and over them that were numbered, brought their offering before the Lord: six covered wagons and twelve oxen, a wagon for two of the princes and for each one an ox.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

points: The Lord told Moses to take the wagons and oxen for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation and give them to the Levites, to every man according to his service: two wagons and four oxen to the sons of Gershon, and four wagons and eight oxen to the sons of Merari, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

points: Unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the sanctuary belonging unto them was that they should bear upon their shoulders. Numbers 4 shows what that bearing was: Aaron and his sons covered the ark and the vessels first, and after that the sons of Kohath came to bear them, not touching any holy thing lest they die.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

points: The princes offered for the dedicating of the altar in the day that it was anointed, and the Lord said unto Moses, they shall offer their offering, each prince on his day.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

points: Nahshon the son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah offered the first day. The charger is simply a plate or a platter, and the bowl and the golden spoon carried the fine flour mingled with oil and the incense.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

points: On the second day Nethaneel the son of Zuar, prince of Issachar, offered. Each prince on his day brought the very same offering as Nahshon, because this was the order that they had to do.

The twelve days went in the order of the camps: Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, Reuben, Simeon, Gad, Ephraim, Manasseh, Benjamin, Dan, Asher, and Naphtali, closing with Ahira the son of Enan on the twelfth day.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

points: This was the dedication of the altar in the day when it was anointed by the princes of Israel, and the totals are summed: twelve chargers of silver, twelve silver bowls, twelve spoons of gold, and all the bullocks, rams, lambs, and goats for the burnt offering, the sin offering, and the peace offerings.

note.label: Numbers 7: The Offering of the Princes at the Dedication of the Altar

When Christ came into the world he said, sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not; the Most High had no pleasure in them, because the people's minds were not changed when they offered them, and Christ was the ultimate sacrifice who took away the first that he might establish the second.
